Spectrea brand audit · D38 · wordmark weight arbitration

Albert Sans 600 or 700 — which is the canonical wordmark?

Everything that renders the wordmark today uses Semibold 600 — the live logo component, the shipped lockup SVGs, and the logo spec. The 700 appears only in the guide's type table and one page mirroring it. This sheet exists to confirm 600 by eye, or to discover you prefer the bolder cut before it's canonized in brand.ts.

pectrea
Flip in place — weight differences read best when nothing else moves. Mark at the shipped proportions (0.72em box, 0.05em gap); the subject is the letterforms.

The S-mark against the letterforms — measured

Constants measured from the repo's Albert Sans variable font at wght 600 (fontkit), against the lockup math in SpectreaLogo.tsx:359-375. The ghost S is the real glyph at true cap-height alignment; the mark overlays it exactly as the lockup scales it.

Real Albert Sans 600 “S” as a teal outline, the current mark over it at the lockup’s own scale. The mark’s 40×58 construction box carries ~1 unit of padding top and bottom, so its ink reads ~3% shorter than the S — that’s real, not a rendering error.

Shape candidates — nudging the mark toward the real S

All candidates use the ratified B constants and the identical rendering method. In each overlay the teal outline is the real S glyph and the dashed grey line is its extracted centerline (medial axis); the mark is drawn over both at the box scale, full opacity. Two measured axes: deviation from the S’s spine (RMS distance between centerlines, share of glyph height) and counter-mouth clearance (the tip-to-spine passage that clogs first, share of ink height): K0 23.3% · K1 26.4% · K3 18.5% · K3′ 18.9% · K3″ 15.2%. A rendered ladder (below) shows all four principal shapes stay readable down to 11px — small-size legibility does not decide this choice; curvature fidelity and gesture do.

K0 — current shape deviation from S spine 6.3% of height · ink aspect 0.58 (S is 0.69)
K1 — S width bowls widened to the S’s aspect, tips keep today’s reach · deviation 4.6%
K3 — S-fit centerline fitted to the S’s medial axis, 3 smooth cubics with shared junction tangents · deviation 1.9%
K3′ — S-fit + shallow trail critic amendment: K3’s spine and top terminal, the tail re-laid level in the terminal band (exit 35° vs K3’s 69°) · deviation 2.4%, all of it the deliberate tail
Why the tail is shallow but the top is not — the asymmetry is deliberate. (1) Extending the top measurably narrows the counter mouth — the K3″ probe below runs the top out along its tangent and drops clearance from 18.9% to 15.2% of ink height — while extending the tail costs nothing above (K3 → K3′: 18.5 → 18.9). (2) The two ends have different jobs: the bottom is the storytelling end — the stroke dissolves at dot 8 and the trailing pair continues the path, so it must read as a level continuation; the top is where the draw starts, carries no dots and no narrative, so it simply resolves into the letterform. (3) The S itself is asymmetric the same way — Albert Sans’s top terminal sits at 22% height, its bottom at 75% — and the mark always was too: a hard start at dot 1, a dissolving end. K3′ aligns the existing asymmetry with the story rather than introducing one.

Measurement correction. An earlier version of this note cited an independent critic’s aperture table (K3 ≈ 11.6% vs ≈ 6.5% for K0/K1) as the decisive legibility case for the S-fit family. Direct geometric measurement did not replicate it: K1’s counter mouth is in fact the widest of the set (26.4%), and the rendered ladder shows every principal candidate readable at 11px. The legibility argument for K3-over-K1 is therefore withdrawn; what remains for the S-fit family is curvature fidelity to the glyph (1.9–2.4% vs K1’s 4.6%) and the critic’s confirmed observations about K3’s tail (fixed in K3′) and K1’s top tip overshooting the glyph’s edge.
K3″ — top-extended probe not a candidate: K3′ with the top run out ~3.8 units along its tangent, to price a symmetric shallow top · mouth clearance 15.2% (vs K3′’s 18.9%) · deviation 3.4%
Small-size ladder mono stroke at 32 / 26 / 18 / 14 / 11 px — all four principal shapes hold a readable S at 11px; legibility does not decide this choice

Animated — the signature draw

Each candidate running the canonical AnimatedLogo loop (SpectreaLogo.tsx): 3 seconds — ease-out draw along the full path, pause, forward dissolve with a 15% trailing fade — full-spectrum stroke (Cobalt → Teal → Amber), grey dots, 48 gradient segments, each mark at its B-derived stroke weight. This is the brand’s motion signature: “the spectrum stroke draws along the S connecting the dots.”

Evidence annex — decisions in progress

Favicon-size reality check K3′ at 16 / 24 / 32 / 64 px, shown at true size then 3× pixel zoom — the dots and their gaps fall below one pixel at 16px, so the “about to connect” idea fuses away regardless of proportions
The proportions scale perfectly — the pixels don’t. A trailing dot is under 2px wide at favicon size and the dot-to-stroke gap is under ¾ of a pixel, which antialiasing fills. At 16px the mark reads as a plain S (mono) or loses its dots entirely (grey). Canon could only fix this via a micro-construction amendment for ≤24px surfaces — the misuse rules forbid every possible fix (no dot-count changes, no stroke-without-dots). Decision: four micro-constructions were explored (next panel) and all rejected; the standard mark scales down as-is.
Micro-construction candidates four ways to carry the dot idea at ≤24px — each row: mono at 16 / 24 / 32 / 64 px, then grey-dot at 16 / 24 / 32 px
The 16px pixels at 8× zoom left to right: M1 mono · M1 grey · M3 mono · M3 grey · M4 mono · M4 grey · M5 mono · M5 grey
Decision (Darren, 2026-08-06): all four rejected. Judged too far from what the actual mark looks like — the standard mark simply scales down unchanged, and its plain-S reading at favicon sizes is accepted. No canon amendment. This panel stays as evidence of the exploration.

M1 — enlarged trailing pair. Stroke shortened to 6.5/9 of the arc; the two trailing dots grow to r 5.5 and are re-spaced so every gap is ≥ 1px at 16px (measured 4.1 and 4.0 units against a 4-unit floor). The full mark’s story — stroke plus two dots about to connect — survives verbatim: at 16px both dots stay separate in mono and grey. Cost: dot size and spacing deviate from the ratified 7:8 constants, which is exactly the deviation the canon amendment would permit below 24px.

M3 — optical bolding (control). Thicken the stroke to 12 and all ten dots to r 6, layout unchanged. Fails: the tail dots sit 0.9–1.1 units apart and fuse into a club foot at every size. This proves the failure is spacing, not weight — thickening alone cannot rescue the ratified layout.

M4 — dotted S. Seven dots, no stroke. Maximum “dots” story, but at 16px the S dissolves into a dice pattern and the grey version nearly vanishes. Identity loss outweighs metaphor gain.

M5 — single trailing spark. Stroke to 7/9 plus one r 6 dot. Cleanest 16px render and unmistakably an S, but the pair — two nodes about to join — reduces to a lone dot: a weaker telling of the same idea.
The hero anchor public/illustrations/hero-example-composition.png — the sole published style exemplar; decision: honest caption pre-push, regenerate in a dedicated art session
Confirmed breaches of its own prompt: all four primaries at 96–100% canonical saturation (the prompt’s explicit reject condition) and neutral-grey supporting forms against the neutral-fill rule (~5.7% of frame). Otherwise a good render — warm, craft-compliant, excellent hue fidelity — and the guide caption currently overclaims a full checklist pass. No brand metaphor present; the co-primary decision routes both metaphors into the content brief with authority in the render path.
What to look for: at hero sizes 700 gains presence but the counters of e and a tighten; at 22px and below 700 starts to clog while 600 keeps the round forms open next to the 8-unit mark stroke. Whichever wins becomes the canonical value in brand.ts; the losing citations get corrected.

Drift note found while verifying this page: the SPA component applies kerning and 0.02em tracking to the wordmark; the asset generator uses raw advances with neither, so the shipped lockup SVGs' wordmark is 0.144em narrower and unkerned vs the live site (generate-brand-assets.mjs:44-49 vs SpectreaLogo.tsx:459). The variants above follow the SPA.
